title: Many Worlds sues OpenAI in ED Texas over five retrieval/personalization/generation patents
claim: IPWatchdog 2026-09-02: Many Worlds 2T Innovations LLC sued OpenAI OpCo, LLC on 2026-08-31 in the Eastern District of Texas (Marshall), alleging infringement of five patents (U.S. 8,676,742; 8,843,433; 10,699,202; 12,307,388; 12,299,603) covering contextual/personalized retrieval, vector search, recommendation, and probabilistic generation. Named products include ChatGPT surfaces plus OpenAI Vector Stores and File Search. Fact is the filing; infringement and eligibility are allegations.

title: ACLE-MCP: short-lived sender-constrained leases for invocation-time MCP trust
claim: arXiv 2609.02690 (ACLE-MCP) binds workload freshness, operation, object, params, downstream, and receipts into a short-lived sender-constrained capability lease at invocation. Author-reported prototype: full ACLE-MCP blocked all evaluated attacks; normal pooled p95 12.20→15.34ms (+25.7%) vs OAuth-only. Narrow author-reported prototype, not a shipped MCP spec. Intersects effect-closure / head-SHA binding.
excerpt: For protected calls, ACLE-MCP issues a short-lived, sender-constrained capability lease that binds the expected workload, freshness requirement, operation, object and parameter bounds, downstream constraints, and receipt obligations. ... full ACLE-MCP blocks all evaluated attack families while preserving all benign tasks. ... the complete design increases request-level pooled p95 latency on normal allowed calls by 25.7% relative to OAuth-only.
suggested_capture: bun run beep research capture https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02690 --tags agents,mcp,leases,attestation
